A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MedVerse framework. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison across pagination and numbering changes.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A report original benchmark accuracy, inference efficiency, data-scaling experiments, and architectural ablations.

after.justification: Original experiments are retained, with additional model-scaling, runtime, topology, and clinical-reliability results.

M1.justification: The curator, topology-aware attention, adaptive positions, and planning/Fork/Join execution remain unchanged. Appendix curator prompts are also retained. The 14B experiment applies the existing method.

E1.justification: Training sources and the five medical benchmark variants remain unchanged. HLE's Medical/Biomed wording changes do not establish different coverage. The 50-case HLE analysis and larger-model evaluation extend evaluation within retained tasks.

E2.justification: New Table 7 adds the original Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct checkpoint as a comparator for MedVerse-14B. Table 1 retains its original-model, MedReason, and Huatuo-o1 comparators, and existing ablation variants are unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a GPT-5.2 judging protocol covering 50 HLE cases and five clinical-reliability metrics, topology-stratified profiling, runtime decomposition, and a 14B-model evaluation. These substantially extend evaluation design; the previously stated training and efficiency settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine pipeline overhead, performance across graph topologies, clinical reasoning errors, and scaling to 14B parameters. Earlier linear-planning, training-data-size, and training/inference ablations are retained; the latter moves from Appendix A.2 to A.3.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The newly stated 50-case sample size concerns evaluation design rather than repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results: 39% planning versus 61% execution time, topology-specific speedups, clinical-reliability scores, and 14B benchmark scores. Table 4 reports high-risk errors of 5.7% for MedVerse versus 11.4% for Serial; Table 7 reports 44.74% average accuracy versus 37.91% for the original 14B model. Existing Table 1 scores remain unchanged, and appendix ablation percentage conversion is equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The DAG/Petri-net definitions, enabled-transition frontier, and attention equations remain unchanged. New empirical discussions do not introduce a substantive mathematical derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract adds an explicit claim of improved clinical reliability alongside comparable performance against specialized medical LLMs, and the conclusion includes reliability among the benefits. The framework contributions and headline accuracy and efficiency claims are retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting reliability gains to Join-based consistency and larger-model gains to structural inductive bias. New limitations explicitly qualify speedups for linear graphs and restrict the evidence to offline evaluation, while the ethics section requires clinical validation and human oversight.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code-availability link, and Section 5.6 explicitly identifies shared MedVerse-14K training data for the retained architectural ablation. Existing training hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and curator prompting details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zheng et al. (2023), Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena, to support its judging approach. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to medical reasoning and parallel-generation methods otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Local additions create structural-analysis, clinical-reliability, ethics, limitations, model-scaling, and LLM-use sections, with updated cross-references and small wording corrections rather than extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: New Tables 2–4 and 7 substantially expand experimental displays with runtime, topology, reliability, and model-scaling comparisons. Existing tables are retained and renumbered, the architectural-ablation table switches to percentages, and Figure 4 is resized and relabeled from Multiverse-Med to MedVerse.

improvement.justification: The runtime and topology diagnostics, 14B evaluation, explicit deployment limitations, and code link improve the paper's assessability beyond v1. However, the clinical claims rely on an incompletely documented 50-case LLM-judge study without uncertainty reporting. Section 5.4 also claims accuracy up to 63.5%, whereas Table 3 reports 54.3% and 56.7%. The added checks and clearer scope provide a useful but limited net improvement.
